messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Incident created — Region: us-west-2 — symptom: elevated ELB 502s + TCP resets observed across multiple AZs. Pager: PagerDuty incident PD-8231.
Li (oncall): seeing spike in synthetic 5xx from edge LB healthcheck ~10:12 UTC. Beginning triage.
Maya (infra-sre): logging in to check target group health and ENI flaps. ETA 5m.
Dan (network): I see increased RSTs on elb-evt logs, path to AZB looks noisy. Possible ENI detach/re-attach wave.
Li (oncall): creating zoom -> zoom.us/j/999999999 (incident bridge). Adding CS for customer comms.
CS_Rep: on it — preparing initial customer note: "We are investigating elevated 502s for some customers in US-WEST-2; mitigation in progress."
Maya (infra-sre): quick checks:
```
# curl to local ELB health
curl -sS -D - https://internal-elb-usw2.example/health || true
# observed: TCP RSTs, intermittent 200s
```
Maya (infra-sre): target groups show 20-30% targets Unhealthy in azb and azc, draining in azd.
Dan (network): route53 health checks still green (edge level) — problem appears downstream of edge resolver, inside AZ networks.
Li (oncall): rolling mitigation plan: 1) reduce per-AZ traffic by adjusting Route53 weights to favor other AZs, 2) enable cross-zone LB balancing and increase healthy thresholds, 3) ask AWS for ENI/EC2 control-plane check.
Maya (infra-sre): running config tweak to lower connection reuse window on proxy layer to avoid conntrack starvation: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=180` (will monitor).
Dan (network): also toggling cross-zone load balancing ON for affected ELBs: applying now.
Li (oncall): Route53 change deployed: shifted 40% weight away from us-west-2 AZB/C -> other healthy AZs in same region temporarily. Propagation visible.
CS_Rep: posted interim customer update: "Traffic rerouted to reduce impact; some requests may see latencies or retries. We'll follow up once stabilized."
Maya (infra-sre): AWS console: I/O to EBS volumes looks fine; no EBS throttling. EC2 control plane shows several ENI detach events correlated with timestamps. Opening AWS support case now. Case: 1234567890.
IncidentBot: AWS Support case 1234567890 opened and linked to PD-8231.
Dan (network): running `tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst) != 0'` on a few hosts — getting bursts from a subset of hosts tied to a specific AZ.
Li (oncall): mitigation #2: scale up healthy capacity in other AZs by +30% (ASG increase) so Route53 weight shift has capacity headroom.
Maya (infra-sre): ASG scale triggered, instances initializing, warming LB targets.
Kate (product): any customer-facing ETA? Need to inform customers with high SLA risk.
CS_Rep: proposing message in 30m if still degraded. Will flag high-risk accounts now.
Dan (network): found pattern: recent kernel module rollout on a set of instances two hours ago (net-accel v2.1). Looks suspicious — that batch is concentrated in azb.
Maya (infra-sre): rolling back net-accel v2.1 on a rolling subset in azb now (rm -rf, kidding — doing proper package revert).
Li (oncall): start rollback and monitor metrics, I'll keep PD status updated.
Maya (infra-sre): rollback step 1/3 complete in azb — target health improving from 60% -> 88% on first host batch.
Dan (network): ENI reattachments dropping dramatically after revert batch 1. RSTs declining.
Li (oncall): good sign. Keeping Route53 weight shifts until azb healthy >95% for 10m.
IncidentBot: Incident severity reduced from P1 -> P2 based on decreased customer impact.
CS_Rep: updated customers: "We identified a faulty kernel/network agent rollout causing instability; we have reverted the rollout in affected AZs and are monitoring. Some services may have experienced transient errors. We'll post a full RCA when complete."
Maya (infra-sre): full revert across azb done. Health: azb 99%, azc 97%, azd 100%.
Dan (network): removing temporary Route53 weight adjustments, restoring original weights. Propagation in progress.
Li (oncall): rolling back sysctl change to default after stability confirmed.
Kate (product): can you draft a short post-incident note for the status page? I'll review.
Maya (infra-sre): AWS support replied: control plane saw transient instance-networking hiccup linked to ENI attach hot path, recommended per-instance networking debug logs collected. Case remains open for postmortem with AWS.
Li (oncall): preparing handoff to night oncall — summary: root cause likely net-accel v2.1 rollout triggered conn/ENI instability in azb; reverted, traffic shifted, ASGs scaled, stability restored. Customers saw increased 502s for ~22 minutes.
Li (oncall): Handoff notes -> monitor ELB 5xx rate, ENI attach metrics, Route53 weight drift. PagerDuty auto-escalation profile adjusted to quiet non-critical front-end alerts for next 60m.
Maya (infra-sre): uploaded debug bundles to S3: s3://rwd-incident/PD-8231/debug-bundles/1839994321.zip
CS_Rep: sending follow-up to impacted customers with post-incident timeline and contact.
PagerDuty: Incident PD-8231 marked acknowledged, awaiting postmortem.
Li (oncall): closing incident channel momentarily — will reopen if metrics regress. Thanks all :heart:.
